prompt:
A single mobile web page screen, portrait, 1024x1536, rendered edge to edge as the page itself (no phone frame, no browser chrome, no hands, no desk). It is "Oozedle", a daily guessing game for a college ultimate frisbee team called Ooze: each day it hides one player's stat line from one tournament and you get six guesses to name the player; after each guess every stat shows only an arrow (up = the hidden player had more, down = fewer) or an equals sign. This is a working game screen built from standard web controls (a text input with autocomplete, a button, a table), not a poster.

Regions, top to bottom:
1. A slim top bar: the wordmark "OOZEDLE" on the left; two text links on the right, "Players" and "Tournaments".
2. The puzzle header: puzzle number "#214", the date "Tue Oct 21", and the puzzle's tournament "PDQ" with its season "2026"; one short line: "Name the player. 6 guesses."
3. The guess table, the focal working area: column heads "Player", "PP", "A", "G", "B", "T" (points played, assists, goals, blocks, turnovers). Three played rows:
   Rowan: PP up, A down, G up, B down, T equals
   Farmer: PP down, A equals, G up, B down, T up
   Colin: PP up, A down, G equals, B equals, T down
   Then three empty ruled rows numbered 4, 5, 6 still to play. Feedback is arrows and equals signs only, no numbers in the stat cells; equal cells are marked by form (filled cell), not only by colour.
4. The guess control, pinned low within thumb reach: a text input with placeholder "Guess a player" and a "Guess" button.
5. The start of the section below, visible at the bottom edge: a small heading "Yesterday" with "Hugo · SVR 2026" and his line "12 PP · 3 A · 2 G · 1 B · 2 T".

All text legible at real phone reading size; restrained, not busy, no decorative clutter, no mascots, no photos of people, no logos other than the wordmark.

Visual world: a jet-age airline ticket wallet translated into a clean web screen: crisp white coupon stock #ffffff, carrier navy #1d2a57, signal red #d2232a for stamps, carbon purple #5b3c88 for struck figures. One dominant move: each played guess is a coupon row with a tabbed head (the guess number and player name in navy airline grotesk caps), its five stat boxes ruled in hairlines with carbon-purple arrows struck into them; wrong guesses carry a small red "VOID" stamp; the three unplayed guesses are blank coupons. The puzzle header reads like a ticket header: "OOZEDLE · PDQ 2026 · No. 214". Flat, no route maps or planes drawn, no paper texture, no shadows beyond a hairline.
